breaking_pattern_statements.text: The spatial and temporal variation in waves and their breaking patterns at the study site were documented.
Large winter swells typically arrive from the northwest and west; however, this area also experiences un-refracted waves out of the southwest during the summer.

The Pleasure Point area in northern Monterey Bay is a complex coastal setting of sea cliffs and small pocket beaches that are influenced by a variable wave climate due to its south-facing orientation.
Wave breaking patterns were documented using a web-based camera system deployed at a private residence on East Cliff Drive.
This video monitoring made it possible to track wave breaking patterns, rip-channel development and potentially infer rock reef and/or sand-bar location(s) under a range of wave and tide conditions.
The video monitoring makes it possible to track wave breaking patterns (FIGURE 13-15), rip channel development and potentially infer sand-bar location(s) under a range of wave conditions.
Note the much larger regions of wave breaking and whitewater (wave bores) as compared to the period of smaller waves shown above in FIGURE 14.
They also provide a basis for calculating potential changes to wave transformations into the shore at Pleasure Point.

breaking_pattern_negative.note: No peel angle, peel direction, peel speed, breaking position, breaker depth or surf-zone width is printed anywhere in the report. The words "peel", "breaker depth", "surf zone width" do not occur. The breaking record is the imagery itself, which the PDF reproduces only as Figs. 13-15.

geometry_statements.text: This provided broad spatial coverage from approximately 0.5 km offshore into water depths of 3-4 m; the shallower portion of the swath bathymetry thus overlapped the deeper portion of the CPS survey.
In total, more than 3,242,199 soundings were acquired during this survey, extending from water depths just less 2 m to more than 21 m (FIGURE 9).
Twenty-five shore-normal and 23 shore-parallel track lines were collected (FIGURE 6). ... Data was collected into water depths less than 1 m and out into depths of more than 12 m.
In total, more than 103,033 data points were acquired during the one day of surveying, extending from mean sea level down to water depths just less than 12 m.

No direct vertical control was available in the study area during the survey. Instead, vertical control was established using observed water levels from the National Ocean Service (NOS, 2007) Tide Station #9413450 located in Monterey Harbor ... the maximum deviation between the reference station and Santa Cruz is approximately 10 cm at full tide range.
These data were then entered into the SEA Swath Processor acquisition software to establish Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) as the vertical datum of the survey.
For reference, NAVD 88 is 0.04 cm below MLLW at the benchmark. [sic: 0.04 m; App. 3 adds 0.043 m]
added 0.043 to grid depth in order to correct for difference between MLLW and NAVD 88.
In January, 2006, data were collected from the intertidal bedrock platform during a period of extremely low tides. This field effort collected data of the seacliff, beach, and intertidal reef.

Because ground-based lidar scanning can be performed with a horizontal look angle, not only is the cliff topography point density much higher that from an airborne platform, but geologic features such as sea caves and wave cut notches can also be captured.

SWATHplus ... Accuracy: 0.1 m or 1% accuracy versus water depth ... Spatial Resolution: 0.2 m raw, 1.0 m processed ... Quantitative Horizontal Positional Accuracy Assessment: +-0.2 m; Quantitative Vertical Positional Accuracy Assessment: +-0.3 m

CPS ... Quantitative Horizontal Positional Accuracy Assessment: +-0.05 m; Quantitative Vertical Positional Accuracy Assessment: +-0.15 m; reasonable variations in water temperature and salinity (not measured), however, can affect depth estimates by as much as 3% of the water depth.
Survey: 10/13/2005 YD286 - 10/14/2005 YD287, 10/17/2005 YD290 - 10/19/005 YD292; Number of Lines: 97 (89 ~straight, 8 shore-parallel); Water depths: 1-22 m
Terrestrial lidar ... Georeferenced Horizontal and Vertical Positional Accuracy Assessment: +-0.50 m; final DEM point spacing 20 cm.

geometry_negative.note: No reef-crest elevation, bench elevation, seawall elevation, profile depth or slope is printed. Figs. 4, 6 and 9 are coverage maps; no cross-shore profile is drawn anywhere in the report. The only bathymetric picture with a depth scale is Fig. 9.

fig11_monthly.method: red error bar column at each monthly tick; mean = bar midpoint, sd = half-span; y scaled by the panel frame (axis min at frame bottom, max at frame top)

check.note: not the same statistic (monthly means are unweighted by burst count) but should agree to ~0.05 m

timex_geometry.lens: Sony FCB-EX480A, 18x zoom, HFOV 48-2.8 deg; zoom state per scene not printed
timex_geometry.controls_available: none in the water plane; the horizon fixes tilt and roll given f; pan and f need >= 2 surveyed land points in frame; the OSM coastline is the bluff base, hidden from a bluff-top camera
timex_geometry.verdict: not digitised: at 250-650 m range the 300-row panel resolves 6-60 m per pixel cross-shore before any pose error, and no control point in the water plane is printed

legend.note: legend labels 1m/3ft (top), 5m/16ft, 10m/33ft, 15m/49ft, 20m/66ft (bottom); label rows equally spaced -> linear

calibration.residual_sign: fig9 - ncei, both metres below MLLW; raw = legend reading, cal = through the ramp fit
calibration.note: NCEI matches the CSMP 2 m soundings to 0.076 m RMS from the 10 m isobath out (BATHY_SOURCES_2026-09-01 §3), so the >= 10 m zone calibrates the digitiser; the ramp fit is then applied unchanged shoreward, where the residual is swath vs interpolant. Readings on a ramp end are bounds, not values.

AWAC.printed_depth_note: transducer depth, App. 4; tide state not stated (+-0.9 m about MSL)

fig9.method: graticule-tick affine (5 lon x 3 lat ticks), hue -> depth through the legend bar, 3x3 median, sampled along the OSM shore-normal through each spot node from the nearest coastline point
